drivingQuestion: How must one conduct himself with modesty in the bathroom, and how far must he distance himself in order to relieve himself?
outcomeNote: Largely a thematic anthology on bathroom conduct; each of its dialectical cycles closes — the two objections against Isi bar Natan are answered (בטהרות הקלו, שאני אוכלי טהרות, and Rav Ashi's reading), and the difficulty against the baraita on modesty is settled both by emendation and by Rav Ashi's restriction to a corner.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: פַּעַם אַחַת נִכְנַסְתִּי אַחַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא, וְלָמַדְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים: לָמַדְתִּי שֶׁאֵין נִפְנִין מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב אֶלָּא צָפוֹן וְדָרוֹם, וְלָמַדְתִּי שֶׁאֵין נִפְרָעִין מְעוּמָּד אֶלָּא מְיוּשָּׁב, וְלָמַדְתִּי שֶׁאֵין מְקַנְּחִין בְּיָמִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׂמֹאל. אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן עַזַּאי: עַד כָּאן הֵעַזְתָּ פָּנֶיךָ בְּרַבְּךָ?! אָמַר לוֹ תּוֹרָה הִיא, וְלִלְמוֹד אֲנִי צָרִיךְ.
segments.en: «It was taught» in a baraita in tractate Derekh Eretz that «Rabbi Akiva said: I once entered the bathroom after» my teacher «Rabbi Yehoshua, and I learned three things from» observing «his» behavior: «I learned that one should not defecate» while facing «east and west, but rather» while facing «north and south; I learned that one should not uncover himself» while «standing, but» while «sitting,» in the interest of modesty; «and I learned that one should not wipe with his right» hand, «but with his left. Ben Azzai,» a student of Rabbi Akiva, «said to him: You were impertinent to your teacher to that extent» that you observed that much? «He replied: It is Torah, and I must learn.»

segments.he: תַּנְיָא, בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: פַּעַם אַחַת נִכְנַסְתִּי אַחַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא, וְלָמַדְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים: לָמַדְתִּי שֶׁאֵין נִפְנִין מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב אֶלָּא צָפוֹן וְדָרוֹם, וְלָמַדְתִּי שֶׁאֵין נִפְרָעִין מְעוּמָּד אֶלָּא מְיוּשָּׁב, וְלָמַדְתִּי שֶׁאֵין מְקַנְּחִין בְּיָמִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׂמֹאל. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: עַד כָּאן הֵעַזְתָּ פָּנֶיךָ בְּרַבְּךָ?! אָמַר לוֹ: תּוֹרָה הִיא, וְלִלְמוֹד אֲנִי צָרִיךְ.
segments.en: Similarly, «we learned» in a baraita: «Ben Azzai said: I once entered a bathroom after Rabbi Akiva, and I learned three things from» observing «his» behavior: «I learned that one should not defecate» while facing «east and west, but rather» while facing «north and south; I learned that one should not uncover himself» while «standing, but» while «sitting; and I learned that one should not wipe with his right» hand, «but with his left. Rabbi Yehuda said to him: You were impertinent to your teacher to that extent? He replied: It is Torah, and I must learn.»

segments.he: רַב כָּהֲנָא עָל, גְּנָא תּוּתֵיהּ פּוּרְיֵיהּ דְּרַב. שַׁמְעֵיהּ דְּשָׂח וְשָׂחַק וְעָשָׂה צְרָכָיו. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דָּמֵי פּוּמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּא כִּדְלָא שָׂרֵיף תַּבְשִׁילָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כָּהֲנָא, הָכָא אַתְּ? פּוּק, דְּלָאו אֹרַח אַרְעָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תּוֹרָה הִיא, וְלִלְמוֹד אֲנִי צָרִיךְ.
segments.en: On a similar note, the Gemara relates that «Rav Kahana entered and lay beneath Rav’s bed. He heard» Rav «chatting and laughing» with his wife, «and seeing to his needs,» i.e., having relations with her. Rav Kahana «said to» Rav: «The mouth» of «Abba,» Rav, «is like» one whom «has never eaten a cooked dish,» i.e., his behavior was lustful. Rav «said to him: Kahana, you are here? Leave, as» this «is an undesirable mode of behavior.» Rav Kahana «said to him: It is Torah, and I must learn.»

segments.he: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין מְקַנְּחִין בְּיָמִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׂמֹאל? אָמַר רָבָא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִיתְּנָה בְּיָמִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מִימִינוֹ אֵשׁ דָּת לָמוֹ״. רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא קְרוֹבָה לַפֶּה. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקּוֹשֵׁר בָּהּ תְּפִילִּין. רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּרְאֶה בָּהּ טַעֲמֵי תוֹרָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Why must one not wipe» himself «with his right» hand, «but with his left? Rava said: Because the Torah was given with the right» hand, «as it is stated: “At His right hand was a fiery law unto them”» (Deuteronomy 33:2). «Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Because» the right hand «is close to the mouth,» i.e., people eat with the right hand. «And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Because one ties the phylacteries» onto his left hand «with» his right hand. «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Because one points to the» cantillation «notes of the Torah with» his right hand.

segments.he: כְּתַנָּאֵי. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאוֹכֵל בָּהּ. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכּוֹתֵב בָּהּ. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּרְאֶה בָּהּ טַעֲמֵי תוֹרָה.
segments.en: The Gemara notes that this is «parallel to a tannaitic» dispute: «Rabbi Eliezer says:» One is forbidden to wipe himself with his right hand «because he eats with it. Rabbi Yehoshua says: Because he writes with it. Rabbi Akiva says: Because he points to the notes of the Torah with it.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי: כׇּל הַצָּנוּעַ בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא נִצּוֹל מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים — מִן הַנְּחָשִׁים, וּמִן הָעַקְרַבִּים, וּמִן הַמַּזִּיקִין. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים אַף חֲלוֹמוֹתָיו מְיוּשָּׁבִים עָלָיו.
segments.en: «Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai said: Anyone who is modest in the bathroom will be saved from three things: From snakes, from scorpions and from demons. And some say» that «even his dreams will be settling for him.»

segments.he: הַהוּא בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא דַּהֲוָה בִּטְבֶרְיָא, כִּי הֲווֹ עָיְילִי בֵּיהּ בֵּי תְרֵי — אֲפִילּוּ בִּימָמָא מִתַּזְּקִי. רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי הֲווֹ עָיְילִי בֵּיהּ חַד וְחַד לְחוֹדֵיהּ — וְלָא מִתַּזְּקִי. אָמְרִי לְהוּ רַבָּנַן: לָא מִסְתְּפֵיתוּ? אָמְרִי לְהוּ: אֲנַן קַבָּלָה גְּמִירִינַן, קַבָּלָה דְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא — צְנִיעוּתָא וּשְׁתִיקוּתָא. קַבָּלָה דְיִסּוּרֵי — שְׁתִיקוּתָא וּמִבְעֵי רַחֲמֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «There was a particular bathroom in» the city of «Tiberias, where, when two would enter it, even during the day, they would be harmed» by demons. When «Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi would each enter alone, they were not harmed. The Sages said to them: Aren’t you afraid?» Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi «said to them: We have learned» through tradition: The «tradition» to avoid danger in the «bathroom» is to conduct oneself with «modesty and silence. The tradition» to end «suffering» is with «silence and prayer.»

segments.he: אַבָּיֵי מְרַבְּיָא לֵיהּ אִמֵּיהּ אִמְּרָא לְמֵיעַל בַּהֲדֵיהּ לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא. וּלְרַבֵּי לֵיהּ גַּדְיָא! שָׂעִיר בְּשָׂעִיר מִיחַלַּף.
segments.en: Because fear of demons in bathrooms was pervasive, the Gemara relates: «Abaye’s mother raised a lamb to accompany him to the bathroom.» The Gemara objects: She should have «raised a goat for him.» The Gemara responds: «A goat» could be «interchanged with a goat-demon.» Since both the demon and the goat are called sa’ir, they were afraid to bring a goat to a place frequented by demons.

segments.he: רָבָא, מִקַּמֵּי דַּהֲוָה רֵישָׁא, מְקַרְקְשָׁא לֵיהּ בַּת רַב חִסְדָּא אַמְגּוּזָא בְּלָקָנָא. בָּתַר דִּמְלַךְ, עֲבַדָא לֵיהּ כַּוְּותָא, וּמַנְּחָא לֵיהּ יְדָא אַרֵישֵׁיהּ.
segments.en: «Before Rava became the head of the yeshiva,» his wife, «the daughter of Rav Ḥisda, would rattle a nut in a copper vessel for him.» This was in order to fend off demons when he was in the bathroom. «After» he was chosen to «preside» as head of the yeshiva, he required an additional degree of protection, so «she constructed a window for him,» opposite where he would defecate, «and placed her hand upon his head.»

segments.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר — נִפְנֶה מִיָּד. וּבַבִּקְעָה, כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ וְאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ. אִיסִי בַּר נָתָן מַתְנֵי הָכִי: אֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר, כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ וְאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ, וּבַבִּקְעָה — כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֵהוּ.
segments.en: With regard to where one may or may not go to defecate, «Ulla said: Behind a fence, one» need not distance himself from people and «may defecate immediately. In a valley» or open field, one must distance himself «sufficiently so that if he passes wind, no one will hear him. Isi bar Natan taught as follows: Behind a fence» one must distance himself «sufficiently so that if he passes wind another does not hear him, and in a valley,» one must distance himself «sufficiently so that no one can see him.»

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: יוֹצְאִין מִפֶּתַח בֵּית הַבַּד, וְנִפְנִין לַאֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר, וְהֵן טְהוֹרִין!
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection» based on what we learned in a mishna in Teharot: Physical laborers, who usually fall into the category of am ha’aretz and are not generally cautious with regard to the laws of ritual purity, «exit from the entrance of the olive press, defecate behind the fence, and are ritually pure.» There is no reason to be concerned that they might become impure in the interim. This indicates that a greater distance is unnecessary.

segments.he: בִּטְהָרוֹת הֵקֵלּוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «With regard to» the laws of «ritual purity, they were lenient.» To ensure maintenance of purity, they were lenient and did not require a greater distance.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: כַּמָּה יַרְחִקוּ וְיִהְיוּ טְהוֹרִין — כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא רוֹאֵהוּ! שָׁאנֵי אוֹכְלֵי טְהָרוֹת, דַּאֲקִילּוּ בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן.
segments.en: «Come and hear» from what we learned: «How far» may workers «distance themselves, and» the fruit and oil «will» remain «pure?» They may distance themselves only «so far that he» still «sees him.» This contradicts the opinion of Isi bar Natan, who required them to distance themselves sufficiently that they may not be seen. The Gemara responds: Those «who eat in purity are different, as the Sages were lenient with them.»

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי ״כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֶה״ דְּקָאָמַר אִיסִי בַּר נָתָן — כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת פֵּרוּעוֹ, אֲבָל לְדִידֵיהּ חָזֵי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said: What is» the meaning of: «So long as another does not see him, which» was the standard that «Isi bar Natan said? Sufficient that another person cannot see his nakedness, although he does see him.»

segments.he: הַהוּא סַפְדָנָא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אֲמַר: ״הַאי צָנוּעַ בְּאוֹרְחוֹתָיו הֲוָה״. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אַתְּ עֲיַילְתְּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא וְיָדְעַתְּ אִי צָנוּעַ אִי לָא? דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין קוֹרִין ״צָנוּעַ״ אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁצָּנוּעַ בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «There was a particular eulogizer who went» to eulogize an important person «in the presence of Rav Naḥman.» Of the deceased, «he said: This» man «was modest in his ways. Rav Naḥman said to him: Did you go to the bathroom with him and know whether or not he was modest? As we learned» in a baraita: «One can only describe as modest one who is modest» even «in the bathroom,» when no one else is there.

segments.he: וְרַב נַחְמָן מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ? מִשּׁוּם דְּתַנְיָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּפְרָעִין מִן הַמֵּתִים כָּךְ נִפְרָעִין מִן הַסַּפְדָנִין, וּמִן הָעוֹנִין אַחֲרֵיהֶן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And what difference» did it make «to Rav Naḥman,» that he was so insistent upon the details of whether or not this man was modest? The Gemara answers: «Because it was taught» in a baraita: «Just as the deceased are punished, so too are the eulogizers and those who answer after them.»The deceased are punished for transgressions committed in their lifetimes. The eulogizers and those who answer are punished for accepting the attribution of virtues that the deceased did not possess.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ צָנוּעַ — זֶה הַנִּפְנֶה בַּלַּיְלָה בַּמָּקוֹם שֶׁנִּפְנָה בַּיּוֹם.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a baraita: «Who is a modest person? One who defecates at night where he defecates during the day,» i.e., who distances himself at night, in order to relieve himself, no less than he distances himself during the day.

segments.he: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם יַנְהִיג אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ שַׁחֲרִית וְעַרְבִית, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא צָרִיךְ לְהִתְרַחֵק! וְתוּ, רָבָא בִּימָמָא הֲוָה אָזֵיל עַד מִיל, וּבְלֵילְיָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ: פַּנּוֹ לִי דּוּכְתָּא בִּרְחוֹבָא דְמָתָא. וְכֵן אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ: חֲזִי מַאן דְּאִיכָּא אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית חֶבְרַיָּא, דְּבָעֵינָא לְמִפְנֵי! לָא תֵּימָא בַּמָּקוֹם, אֶלָּא אֵימָא: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנִּפְנָה בַּיּוֹם.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «Is that so? Didn’t Rav Yehuda say» that «Rav said: One must always accustom himself» to defecate «in the morning and at night,» when it is dark, «so that he will not need to distance himself? Moreover, during the day, Rava would go up to a mil» outside the city, «and at night he would tell his servant: Clear a place for me in the city street. And so too, Rabbi Zeira told his servant: See who is behind the study hall, as I need to defecate.» These Sages did not defecate at night in the same place where they defecated during the day. «Rather,» emend the statement and «say» as follows: «In the manner that one defecates during the day,» i.e. he should conduct himself at night with the same degree of modesty with which he removes his clothing when defecating during the day.

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בַּמָּקוֹם, לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְקֶרֶן זָוִית.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said: Even if you say» that the text can remain as it was: «Where he defecates during the day,» it «was only necessary in» the case of «a corner,» where one may conceal himself. In the interest of modesty, he should go around the corner at night, just as he does during the day.

segments.he: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם יַנְהִיג אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ שַׁחֲרִית וְעַרְבִית, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא צָרִיךְ לְהִתְרַחֵק.
segments.en: The Gemara discusses «the matter itself. Rav Yehuda said» that «Rav said: One must always accustom himself» to defecate early «in the morning and» late «at night so that he will not need to distance himself.»

segments.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי, בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: הַשְׁכֵּם וָצֵא, הַעֲרֵב וָצֵא, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְרַחֵק. מַשְׁמֵשׁ וָשֵׁב, וְאַל תֵּשֵׁב וּתְמַשְׁמֵשׁ, שֶׁכָּל הַיּוֹשֵׁב וּמְמַשְׁמֵשׁ — אֲפִילּוּ עוֹשִׂין כְּשָׁפִים בְּאַסְפַּמְיָא, בָּאִין עָלָיו.
segments.en: «That» opinion «was also taught» in a baraita: «Ben Azzai said: Rise early» in the morning «and go» defecate, wait for «evening and go» defecate, «so that you will not» need to «distance yourself.» He also said: «Touch» around the anus first to assist in the opening of orifices «and» then «sit; do not sit and» then «touch, for anyone who sits and» then «touches, even if sorcery is performed in» a distant place like «Aspamia,» the sorcery «will come upon him.»

segments.he: וְאִי אִנְּשִׁי וִיתִיב וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַשְׁמֵשׁ, מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ? — כִּי קָאֵי, לֵימָא הָכִי: ״לָא לִי לָא לִי, לָא תַּחִים וְלָא תַּחְתִּים, לָא הָנֵי וְלָא מֵהָנֵי, לָא חַרְשֵׁי דְחַרָּשָׁא וְלָא חַרְשֵׁי דְחַרָּשְׁתָא״.
segments.en: The Gemara says: «And if one forgets and sits and then touches, what is his remedy? When» he «stands,» he should «recite the following» incantation: «Not for me, not for me, neither taḥim nor taḥtim,» types of sorcery, «neither these nor from these, neither the sorcery of a sorcerer nor the sorcery of a sorceress.»

segments.he: תַּנְיָא, בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: עַל כׇּל מִשְׁכָּב שְׁכַב, חוּץ מִן הַקַּרְקַע. עַל כׇּל מוֹשָׁב שֵׁב, חוּץ מִן הַקּוֹרָה. אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שֵׁינָה בְּעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר כְּאִסְטָמָא לְפַרְזְלָא. יְצִיאָה בְּעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר כְּאִסְטָמָא לְפַרְזְלָא.
segments.en: Continuing with the subject of health, «it was taught» in a baraita: «Ben Azzai says: On all beds, lie, except for the ground. On all seats, sit, except for a beam,» lest you fall off. «Shmuel said: Sleeping at dawn is» as effective «as forging [istema]» is «to iron. A» bowel «movement at dawn» is as beneficial «as forging» is «to iron.»

segments.he: בַּר קַפָּרָא הֲוָה מְזַבֵּן מִילֵּי בְּדִינָרֵי: עַד דְּכָפְנַתְּ — אֱכוֹל. עַד דְּצָחֵית — שְׁתִי, עַד דְּרָתְחָא קִדְרָךָ — שְׁפוֹךְ. קַרְנָא קָרְיָא בְּרוֹמִי, בַּר מְזַבֵּין תְּאֵנֵי, תְּאֵנֵי דַּאֲבוּךְ זַבֵּין.
segments.en: Similarly, the Gemara relates: «Bar Kappara would sell sayings for dinars;» he would express his ideas in brief maxims. For example: «If you are hungry, eat;» do not delay eating, as the hunger may pass and your food will be of no benefit. So too, «if you are thirsty, drink; while the pot is still boiling, pour it» out before it cools off. This is a metaphor for relieving oneself. Bar Kappara also said: «When the horn is sounded in Rome,» signifying that there is demand for figs in the Roman market, «son of a fig seller, sell your father’s figs,» even without his permission, so as not to miss the opportunity.

segments.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּנָן: כִּי עָיְילִיתוּ בִּשְׁבִילֵי דְמָחוֹזָא לְמִיפַּק בֵּיהּ בְּחַקְלָא, לָא תֶּחֱזוֹ לָא לְהַךְ גִּיסָא וְלָא לְהַךְ גִּיסָא, דִּלְמָא יָתְבֵי נְשֵׁי, וְלָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְאִסְתַּכּוֹלֵי בְּהוּ.
segments.en: «Abaye said to the Sages: When you enter the paths» of the city of «Meḥoza in order to go out» and defecate «in a field, look neither to one side nor to the other, as perhaps women are sitting there and it is improper to look at them.»

segments.he: רַב סָפְרָא עָל לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא. אֲתָא רַבִּי אַבָּא, נְחַר לֵיהּ אַבָּבָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֵיעוּל מָר. בָּתַר דִּנְפַק אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד הַשְׁתָּא לָא עֲיַילְתְּ לְשֵׂעִיר, וּגְמַרְתְּ לָךְ מִילֵּי דְשֵׂעִיר! לָאו הָכִי תְּנַן: מְדוּרָה הָיְתָה שָׁם וּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁל כָּבוֹד. וְזֶה הָיָה כְּבוֹדוֹ: מְצָאוֹ נָעוּל — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם אָדָם, מְצָאוֹ פָּתוּחַ — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁאֵין שָׁם אָדָם. אַלְמָא לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא הוּא!
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «Rav Safra once entered a bathroom,» when «Rabbi Abba came along.» To determine if he could enter, Rabbi Abba «coughed next to the door.» Rav Safra «said to him: Enter, master. When he came out, Rabbi Abba said to him: Until now, you never entered Seir,» the land of the Edomites, who are not strict in their practice of modesty, «and» yet «you» already «learned the» customs of «Seir? Didn’t we learn» in the mishna concerning the Temple: «There was a fire» next to the ritual bath, «and a bathroom of honor. And this was its honor: If one found it locked, it was known that someone was inside;» if «he found it open, it was known that no one was inside.» Speaking in the bathroom «is not a desired mode of behavior».

segments.he: וְהוּא סָבַר מְסוּכָּן הוּא. דְּתַנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: עַמּוּד הַחוֹזֵר מֵבִיא אֶת הָאָדָם לִידֵי הִדְרוֹקָן. סִילוֹן הַחוֹזֵר מֵבִיא אֶת הָאָדָם לִידֵי יֵרָקוֹן.
segments.en: The Gemara explains the opinion of Rav Safra, who told Rabbi Abba that he could enter while in the bathroom: Rav Safra «held that it was dangerous» for Rabbi Abba. If he waited and was uncertain whether or not he could enter, he would endanger himself. «As it was taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says: A column» of feces «that is held back» because one cannot relieve himself «causes dropsy [hidrokan]. A stream [silon]» of urine «that is held back causes jaundice.»

segments.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר עָל לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא. אֲתָא הַהוּא רוֹמָאָה דַּחֲקֵיהּ. קָם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וּנְפַק. אֲתָא דְּרָקֹונָא שַׁמְטֵיהּ לְכַרְכְּשֵׁיהּ. קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: ״וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּיךָ״, אַל תִּקְרֵי ״אָדָם״ אֶלָּא ״אֱדוֹם״.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «Rabbi Elazar entered a bathroom. This Roman came and pushed him» away. «Rabbi Elazar stood and left,» and «a serpent came and ripped out the intestines» of the Roman. «Rabbi Elazar recited the» following «verse about» the Roman: «“Therefore I will give man [adam] for you”» (Isaiah 43:4); «do not read» it as «adam, but rather read» it as «Edom,» meaning a Roman.

moves.cueHe: אמר לו בן עזאי: עד כאן העזת פניך ברבך
moves.summary: Ben Azzai objects that observing one's teacher that closely is impertinence
moves.about: whether following one's teacher into the bathroom and observing him is impertinence

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: תורה היא וללמוד אני צריך
moves.summary: Rabbi Akiva answers that it is Torah and he is obliged to learn it
moves.about: why observing his teacher was legitimate — it is Torah and he must learn it

moves.cueHe: תניא
moves.summary: a baraita: Rabbi Akiva followed Rabbi Yehoshua into the bathroom and learned three rules of conduct
moves.about: brings the baraita of Rabbi Akiva's three lessons learned in the bathroom

moves.cueHe: תניא, בן עזאי אומר
moves.summary: a parallel baraita in which Ben Azzai reports the same three lessons from Rabbi Akiva and is rebuked by Rabbi Yehuda
moves.about: brings the parallel baraita in which Ben Azzai reports the same three lessons from Rabbi Akiva

moves.cueHe: רב כהנא על, גנא תותיה פורייה דרב
moves.summary: Rav Kahana lies beneath Rav's bed and criticizes his conduct with his wife
moves.about: Rav Kahana lying beneath Rav's bed in order to observe him

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: כהנא, הכא את? פוק, דלאו ארח ארעא
moves.summary: Rav tells Rav Kahana to leave, since this is not proper conduct
moves.about: whether hiding under one's teacher's bed to observe him is proper behaviour

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: תורה היא, וללמוד אני צריך
moves.summary: Rav Kahana answers, as Rabbi Akiva did, that it is Torah and he must learn it
moves.about: why lying under Rav's bed was legitimate — it is Torah and he must learn it

moves.cueHe: מפני מה אין מקנחין בימין אלא בשמאל
moves.summary: the Gemara asks the reason for the third of the baraita's rules
moves.about: the reason for the baraita's rule that one wipes with the left hand and not the right

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: מפני שהתורה ניתנה בימין
moves.summary: Rava: because the Torah was given with the right hand, as the verse says
moves.about: the reason the right hand is reserved — the Torah was given with the right hand

moves.cueHe: רבה בר בר חנה אמר: מפני שהיא קרובה לפה
moves.summary: Rabba bar bar Ḥana: because the right hand is the one used for eating
moves.about: the reason the right hand is reserved — it is the hand near the mouth, used for eating

moves.cueHe: ורבי שמעון בן לקיש אמר: מפני שקושר בה תפילין
moves.summary: Reish Lakish: because one ties the phylacteries with the right hand
moves.about: the reason the right hand is reserved — one ties the phylacteries with it

moves.cueHe: רב נחמן בר יצחק אמר: מפני שמראה בה טעמי תורה
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: because one points to the Torah's cantillation notes with it
moves.about: the reason the right hand is reserved — one points to the Torah's cantillation notes with it

moves.cueHe: כתנאי
moves.summary: the four amoraic reasons are mapped onto a parallel tannaitic dispute of R' Eliezer, R' Yehoshua and R' Akiva
moves.about: brings a tannaitic dispute over the same question of why the right hand is reserved

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי תנחום בר חנילאי
moves.summary: one who is modest in the bathroom is saved from snakes, scorpions and demons; some add that his dreams are settled
moves.about: what one who is modest in the bathroom is saved from — some add that his dreams too will be settled for him

moves.cueHe: ההוא בית הכסא דהוה בטבריא
moves.summary: R' Ami and R' Asi enter the haunted Tiberias bathroom unharmed, protected by modesty and silence
moves.about: entering the haunted Tiberias bathroom singly and coming to no harm

moves.cueHe: אביי מרביא ליה אמיה אמרא
moves.summary: Abaye's mother raised a lamb to accompany him to the bathroom, because of the demons
moves.about: a lamb raised so that Abaye would not be alone in the bathroom

moves.cueHe: שעיר בשעיר מיחלף
moves.summary: a goat (sa'ir) could be confused with a goat-demon (sa'ir)
moves.about: why a goat was avoided — a goat could be confused with a goat-demon, both called שעיר

moves.cueHe: ולרביא ליה גדיא
moves.summary: the Gemara objects that she should have raised a goat
moves.about: why a lamb rather than a goat was raised to accompany him

moves.cueHe: רבא, מקמי דהוה רישא
moves.summary: Rava's wife guarded him in the bathroom, more elaborately once he became head of the yeshiva
moves.about: the protective measures taken for Rava in the bathroom before and after he became head of the yeshiva

moves.cueHe: אמר עולא: אחורי הגדר — נפנה מיד
moves.summary: Ulla fixes the distances: behind a fence, at once; in a valley, out of earshot
moves.about: how far one must distance himself to relieve himself behind a fence and in an open valley

moves.cueHe: איסי בר נתן מתני הכי
moves.summary: Isi bar Natan teaches stricter measures: behind a fence, out of earshot; in a valley, out of sight

moves.cueHe: מיתיבי
moves.summary: objection from the mishna: workers defecate behind the fence and remain pure, so no greater distance is needed
moves.about: whether one behind a fence must distance himself beyond earshot, as Isi bar Natan required

moves.cueHe: בטהרות הקלו
moves.summary: the Sages were lenient in matters of purity, so that case proves nothing
moves.about: why the workers may stay close — in matters of ritual purity the Sages were lenient

moves.cueHe: שאני אוכלי טהרות, דאקילו בהו רבנן
moves.summary: those who eat in purity are a special case in which the Sages were lenient
moves.about: why the workers' standard is no proof — those who eat in purity are a special case in which the Sages were lenient

moves.cueHe: תא שמע
moves.summary: a second objection: workers may distance themselves only so far that they can still be seen
moves.about: whether one in a valley must distance himself beyond sight, as Isi bar Natan required

moves.cueHe: רב אשי אמר: מאי ״כל זמן שאין חברו רואה״ דקאמר איסי בר נתן
moves.summary: Rav Ashi answers instead by narrowing Isi's standard to not being seen uncovered
moves.about: resolving the objection from the workers' distance by narrowing Isi bar Natan's standard to being seen uncovered

moves.cueHe: ההוא ספדנא דנחית קמיה דרב נחמן
moves.summary: a eulogizer calls the deceased modest and Rav Naḥman challenges how he could know
moves.about: a eulogizer praising the deceased as modest in his ways before Rav Naḥman

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב נחמן: את עיילת בהדיה לבית הכסא
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman: only one modest in the bathroom is called modest, and you were not there
moves.about: whether the eulogizer could know that the deceased was modest, since modesty is measured in the bathroom

moves.cueHe: ורב נחמן מאי נפקא ליה מיניה
moves.summary: why did Rav Naḥman care whether the eulogy was accurate?
moves.about: why Rav Naḥman cared whether the eulogy was accurate

moves.cueHe: משום דתניא
moves.summary: because eulogizers and those who answer them are punished along with the dead
moves.about: why Rav Naḥman insisted — eulogizers are punished for virtues falsely attributed to the dead

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן
moves.summary: a baraita defines the modest man as one who defecates at night in the place he does by day
moves.about: the baraita defining the modest man as one who defecates at night where he defecates by day

moves.cueHe: איני?! והאמר רב יהודה אמר רב
moves.summary: against the baraita: Rav's advice and the practice of Rava and R' Zeira show one does not go as far at night
moves.about: whether one really defecates at night in the same place as by day, given Rav's advice and the practice of Rava and Rabbi Zeira

moves.cueHe: לא תימא ״במקום״ אלא אימא ״כדרך שנפנה ביום״
moves.summary: emend the baraita: not in the same place but in the same modest manner
moves.about: adduces Rav Yehuda's tradition from Rav as material for the difficulty

moves.cueHe: רב אשי אמר: אפילו תימא במקום
moves.summary: Rav Ashi keeps the wording and restricts the baraita to a place with a corner to hide behind
moves.about: keeping the baraita's wording by restricting it to a place where there is a corner to hide behind

moves.cueHe: גופא
moves.summary: the sugya returns to Rav Yehuda's dictum in Rav's name in its own right
moves.about: returning to the dictum of Rav Yehuda in Rav's name to treat it in its own right

moves.cueHe: תניא נמי הכי
moves.summary: a baraita of Ben Azzai supports Rav: go out early and late so as not to need distance
moves.about: the baraita of Ben Azzai: rise early and go out, wait for evening and go out

moves.cueHe: ואי אנשי ויתיב ואחר כך משמש, מאי תקנתיה
moves.summary: what remedy is there for one who forgot Ben Azzai's warning and sat before touching?
moves.about: the remedy for one who forgot and sat first and only then touched, against Ben Azzai's warning

moves.cueHe: כי קאי, לימא הכי
moves.summary: on standing he recites the incantation against sorcery
moves.about: the remedy — on standing he recites the incantation against sorcery

moves.cueHe: תניא, בן עזאי אומר
moves.summary: a further baraita of Ben Azzai on where to lie and sit, and Shmuel on sleep and relief at dawn
moves.about: the baraita of Ben Azzai on where to lie and where to sit

moves.cueHe: אמר שמואל: שינה בעמוד השחר כאסטמא לפרזלא
moves.summary: sleep and relief at dawn are as beneficial as tempering is to iron

moves.cueHe: בר קפרא הוה מזבן מילי בדינרי
moves.summary: Bar Kappara's maxims, including not to delay relieving oneself
moves.about: Bar Kappara selling maxims for dinars, among them the advice not to delay relieving oneself

moves.cueHe: אמר להו אביי לרבנן
moves.summary: Abaye instructs the Sages not to look aside on the paths of Meḥoza, lest women be sitting there
moves.about: not looking to either side when going out through the paths of Meḥoza to relieve oneself in the field

moves.cueHe: רב ספרא על לבית הכסא
moves.summary: Rav Safra invites Rabbi Abba in while inside the bathroom, and is reproached for it
moves.about: Rav Safra speaking from inside the bathroom to invite Rabbi Abba in

moves.cueHe: לאו הכי תנן: מדורה היתה שם
